title: dev-13: Behavioral test suite
description: Implement CooklangParserTests.swift using Swift Testing (import Testing, @Test, #expect). Cover every behavioral requirement in the spec: empty input, named ingredient, ingredient+timer with quantity, cookware, metadata parsing, line comments, single-line block comments, multi-line block comments, section headers, malformed input, all quantity table rows, all error cases from the quantity section, and parser determinism. Load .cook fixtures via Bundle.module.
acceptance_criteria: All @Test functions use #expect assertions, not XCTest.
Empty-input test: parse returns Recipe with all arrays empty and metadata.allEntries empty.
@salt parses to one Ingredient named 'salt' with quantity nil.
'Cook @chicken breast{500%g} for ~{10%minutes}.' produces one Ingredient named 'chicken breast' with quantity 500g and one Timer with quantity 10 minutes.
#large bowl{} produces one Cookware named 'large bowl'.
Metadata test: servings and course keys present, metadata lines absent from steps.
Line comment test: comment text stripped, preceding text retained.
Single-line block comment test: text before and after [-...-] concatenated.
Multi-line block comment test: spanned region excised; @ingredient inside comment absent from Recipe.ingredients.
Section test: 'Sauce' section with exactly one step.
Malformed input test (@{}) throws CooklangError.parse with non-empty message and valid line/column.
Every row in the quantity table has a corresponding @Test.
Each error case (empty name, empty value + unit, double %) has a @Test asserting CooklangError.parse is thrown.
Determinism test: parse called twice returns equal Recipe values.
swift test from Packages/CookbookCore/ passes with all tests green.
